Welcome. Have you ever reached a point where your usual routines or beliefs just don’t bring the comfort they used to? Maybe you’ve felt that quiet uncertainty settle in, nudging you to look for something new—something more. If so, you’re not alone. Together, let’s step into that space of not-knowing and see what we might discover.
As we journey through times of change, there’s a mix of vulnerability and hope. Sure, it can feel unsettling when old patterns start to slip away and the future looks a little unclear. But what if that’s not a bad thing? In her book, I Guess I Haven't Learned That Yet: Discovering New Ways of Living When the Old Ways Stop Working, Shauna Jeffs invites us to lean into these moments—encouraging a gentle curiosity about life’s unanswered questions and unresolved challenges.
Through honest storytelling and heartfelt reflection, Shauna shows us how letting go of certainty can actually open doors—doors to growth, resilience, and even unexpected joy. As we listen to her stories and insights, we’ll get to explore what it means to unlearn, to relearn, and to find more authentic ways of connecting with ourselves and with the people around us.
So, let’s approach this together with open minds and open hearts. We might just find that not having all the answers isn’t something to fear. In fact, it could be the very beginning of something new—and truly meaningful.
